title: Replacement of the Onboard Loadable Software Management Module

ata.title: Software Loading — Onboard Loadable Software Management

abstract: The software management module is replaced by a unit with four times the storage and a signed-package loader, so that a full aircraft software configuration can be staged on board before a maintenance window rather than loaded piecemeal.

sections.reason: The original module was specified when a full aircraft software configuration was a fraction of its present size, and it can no longer hold more than two pending loads at once. Operators doing a multi-system update have to make several visits to the aircraft with a portable loader, and the manufacturer of the original module issued an obsolescence notice for the memory device in 2022 with a last-time-buy date in 2025. Both drivers pointed at the same answer.
sections.description: The management module YST726849-60 is replaced by a unit with four times the non-volatile storage and hardware support for signed load packages, so that the integrity check happens on board instead of on the loader. The flight deck control panel D4240123411827 is replaced by a version with a package staging page and a load history display. Pan head screws LN3340K2 hold the new module in the same rack position; no rack change is needed. Detail is on drawing D42401292851. The transceiver 96CQ8 and the loading module 7CQ are re-cabled to the new connector pinout. Work is in zones 116 and 165. The data loading configuration itself is not changed by this modification, only the on-board storage and the integrity mechanism.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 1.9 kg per aircraft. Electrical load reduced by 45 VA. Not interchangeable: the signed package format is not readable by the original module and the connector pinout differs. Software loading tasks throughout the maintenance documentation require reissue because the staging step is new. Aircraft software configuration reporting to the operator changes format, which needs coordination with the operator maintenance system.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00451 in November 2024. Retrofit is available through Service Bulletin MRD-42-1013 and takes one shift with two people; the driver for most operators is the last-time-buy date on the original memory device rather than the extra capacity.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN M00451, supplier module change with a last-time-buy on the previous memory device

title: Replacement of the Onboard Loadable Software Management Module

issue.reason: Single avionics bay embodiment window agreed with the rack replacement standard and one combined loading path validation substituted for two.

Aircraft software configuration reporting to the operator changes format, which needs coordination with the operator maintenance system. The module sits in the same avionics bay zone as the maintenance computer rack and loads through the path that the rack replacement of MOD-165240 re-terminates, so the loading path validation is common to both changes and does not have to be run twice when they are embodied together.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00451 in November 2024. Retrofit is available through Service Bulletin MRD-42-1013 and takes one shift with two people; the driver for most operators is the last-time-buy date on the original memory device rather than the extra capacity. Where the aircraft is also planned for the maintenance computer rack replacement of MOD-165240, the two are booked into one avionics bay window: the bay is opened once, the module and the rack are changed in the same visit and a single loading path validation is run at the end. An operator that takes the module change first on an aircraft already scheduled for the rack change gains nothing and pays for a second bay opening and a second validation.
